stemMd: Two equal masses of the same liquid at 20 °C and 60 °C are mixed in an insulated container of negligible heat capacity. No phase change occurs. What is the final temperature?
explanationMd: Equal masses and equal specific heat mean equal temperature changes in opposite directions. If final temperature is T, heat balance gives T − 20 = 60 − T, so T = 40 °C. Insulation prevents net heat loss from the combined system.

distractorRationale.e: Equal heat capacities give equal weighting, not a bias toward the colder portion.
distractorRationale.a: This biases the result toward the warmer portion without a mass or heat-capacity difference.
distractorRationale.d: Adding temperatures does not conserve thermal energy.
distractorRationale.c: The warmer liquid transfers heat to the colder one.
